summary: The note describes the Suez Canal, an artificial sea-level waterway in Egypt linking the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea through the Isthmus of Suez. It was built by the Suez Canal Company between 1859 and 1869 and officially opened on 17 November 1869. The canal shortens sea routes between the North Atlantic and northern Indian Oceans by roughly 7,000 kilometres, and it carried 17,225 vessels in 2012.
one_line: Egypt's artificial sea-level waterway joining the Mediterranean and Red Seas, built 1859-1869 and shortening Atlantic-to-Indian Ocean shipping routes.
key_facts: The Suez Canal is an artificial sea-level waterway in Egypt connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea through the Isthmus of Suez.
The Suez Canal was constructed by the Suez Canal Company between 1859 and 1869.
Construction of the Suez Canal began on September 25, 1859.
The Suez Canal was officially opened on 17 November 1869.
The canal reduces the journey between the North Atlantic and northern Indian Oceans by approximately 7,000 kilometres (4,300 mi) by avoiding the South Atlantic and southern Indian oceans.
The Suez Canal runs from the northern terminus of Port Said to the southern terminus of Port Tewfik at the city of Suez.
The length of the Suez Canal is 193.30 km (120.11 mi), including its northern and southern access channels.
The original length of the Suez Canal was 102 mi or 164 km.
The Suez Canal has no locks.
The maximum boat beam for the Suez Canal is 77.5 m (254 ft 3 in).
The Suez Canal is navigated under the authority of the Suez Canal Authority.
The original owner of the Suez Canal was the Suez Canal Company (Compagnie Universelle du Canal Maritime de Suez).
In 2012, 17,225 vessels traversed the Suez Canal, an average of 47 per day.
